A.input: exact final immutable .kdna container bytes after Core admission
A.normalization: NONE; do not unpack/repack, canonicalize ZIP or remove signature
A.observation: Core computes from the single captured final byte sequence

C.entry_name_rule: Nonempty strict UTF-8 Unicode scalar path, <=4096 bytes, no control/NUL/backslash/absolute/empty/dot/dot-dot segments or trailing slash. Unique exact name bytes; no Unicode normalization. Sort by unsigned UTF-8 bytes.
C.json_entries: Every admitted name ending exactly .json is strict UTF-8 JSON, no duplicate keys at any depth, no invalid Unicode/nonfinite number; RFC8785 JCS bytes. Other admitted entries are binary exact bytes (including payload.kdnab); no guessing by content.
C.manifest_removal_rule: In kdna.json only, remove those properties if present, retain parent objects and every other property. A present /authoring must be an object under Core admission. Never recursively remove another content_digest key.
C.exclusion_rule: checksums/signature are delivery integrity evidence, not content leaves. build-receipt/reports/authoring are forbidden by runtime admission before hashing, not a route for hiding extra entries. All other admitted runtime and attachment entries are included.
C.cycle_rule: C excludes checksums/signature and the two manifest self-references; E can therefore include the final manifest containing C without a C→E→C cycle.
C.framing: ASCII KDNA-CONTENT-TREE + NUL + ASCII 0.2.0 + NUL + u32be(count); for each sorted included entry: u32be(nameByteLength) + nameUTF8 + u8(kind: JSON=0,binary=1) + u64be(contentByteLength) + canonicalJSONorExactBinary. Count/length overflow rejects; never concatenation without framing.

E.input: exact raw entry bytes for kdna.json, payload.kdnab and manifest runtime.mandatory_entries
E.set_rule: New manifest runtime.mandatory_entries is required, a duplicate-free array of valid existing entry names; required base names need not be repeated. Union with the two base entries, sort unsigned UTF-8 bytes. Missing referenced member rejects. Mandatory declarations cannot include checksums.json, signature.kdsig, mimetype or forbidden authoring entries.
E.normalization: NONE: retain raw JSON whitespace/member ordering and exact payload/attachment bytes; set membership comes from admitted manifest, never from checksums expected digest
E.framing: ASCII KDNA-RUNTIME-ENTRY-SET + NUL + ASCII 0.2.0 + NUL + u32be(count); each sorted entry: u32be(nameByteLength) + nameUTF8 + u64be(rawByteLength) + rawBytes. Same entry-name/overflow rules as C.
E.expected_rule: checksums declaration is expected comparison only; cannot supply observed E

P.input: exact complete admitted Runtime Capsule 0.2 object
P.normalization: RFC8785 JCS, strict JSON/Unicode and duplicate-key rejection before object construction
P.self_reference_rule: P is outside Capsule, never embedded and never computed by removing fields.
P.comparison: Producer computes detached P; trusted delivery evidence carries that P; Host independently recomputes P over received Capsule. All three values (producer, delivery, Host observed) must agree before matched; supplied strings do not create a Host observation.

definition.const: Explicit adoption of KDNA public component semantics 1.0.0.
Static component adoption record for KDNA public component semantics 1.0.0.
Authored method field presence for KDNA public component semantics 1.0.0.

non_schema_rules.requirement: Validate Unicode scalar sequences and UTF-8 limits (Identifier256, entry4096); reject duplicate JSON keys/nonfinite values before parsing loses evidence; validate real UTC calendar/time semantics. JSON Schema maxLength counts characters, not bytes.
Implement the exact A/C/E/P definitions in digest_profiles. Equality comparison states must match observed vs independently sourced expected. Shape checking never computes a digest.
non_schema_rules.future_boundary: digest admission and Host received-Capsule observation

non_schema_rules.requirement: Unique identities; all actor, judgment, result, reason, source, resource, material, relation and dependency references resolve with the declared role within the same admitted asset. No cross-asset semantic merge. Mandatory closure includes upstream dependencies, boundary/result/provenance facts; cycles are retained or rejected by declared semantic validity, never silently truncated.

Result contract/ref/type/recursive value shape and cardinality agree; maximum >= minimum; named result/record fields unique; reserved/unknown states are declarations, not evaluated success. Formation output must bind the judgment result contract. No executing condition text or external evaluator during static interpretation.

Core requiredness is distinct from Writer sufficiency and true confirmation. Never synthesize highest_question/worldview/value_order/role/boundary. Missing declarations remain observed missing; unknown/none/not_applicable and omission are not interchangeable.

non_schema_rules.requirement: Apply accepted R04 exact first-error order and safe correlation. Schema failure is not an admission diagnostic oracle. Retain unsupported tuple as safe branded pending version rejection before mode; do not serialize a brand or coerce/default request_id/budget.

Accepted R02/R06 four-channel algebra: trusted control limit only for admission rejection; lawful UInt only for Envelope; preserve semantic cause independently of actual delivery. READ_ADMISSION_RESPONSE_TOO_SMALL only input-invalid cause; READ_RESPONSE_BUDGET_TOO_SMALL only admitted request. Control values are not recursively budgeted bodies.

non_schema_rules.future_boundary: complete final-body encoder and budget selection

Every external content disclosure freshly rechecks current Host identity/task/clock/revocation/scope; issue<expiry, max1h, rotation on restart; issued-handle record equality, current tuple, A/C/snapshot and selection. Serialized fields never grant authority. No global persistent revocation/PKI implementation here.

Apply R03 whole_asset/catalog/exact_selection/expand projection, mandatory closure and explicit omissions; no unauthorized identity leaks even via catalog/omission/provenance. Root is pure, no I/O/Host/clock; no raw payload/paths/Prompt/DOM. Node captures one byte snapshot, browser needs explicit Core capability.

non_schema_rules.requirement: Ready requires Core valid/static complete/read permission allowed/delivery delivered with Host timestamp; rejection retains only independently observed states and no disclosure. non_schema_rules.future_boundary: state correlation after independently observed stages

Unknown critical container or encryption semantics reject or block Core interpretation; metadata shape grants no cryptographic capability.

Exact finite component_semantics definition including public mapping, native/digest/reference/aggregate binding and limits; public Core resolves once after structural checks. Creation verifies actual external one-use context separately.

host_retained_session_profile.status: normative-profile; implementation and independent acceptance remain separate
host_retained_session_profile.authority: This object is the sole normative source of the retained Host session profile. The Read contract explains it; generated source digests bind it without adding wire fields or executable schema.

activation.scope: One long-lived Host instance, one actual same-Core immutable snapshot, one original trusted Host provider and its Read-owned private issuance registry, one fixed trusted embedding binding.
activation.unsupported_adapter: Next retained sessions MUST reject as unsupported; returning a generic Response is not a server finish event.

binding.trusted_origin: The embedding fixes binding_id, authorization_domain_id and trusted context verification. Client session_id, form data, headers, response claims and transport association metadata cannot establish or replace this binding.
binding.foreign_context: An unrelated or unverified context rejects that call without closing the legitimate bound session. A trusted revocation of the bound context closes the session.
binding.identity: Retain the actual snapshot object issued by the same Core instance and the original provider. An inspected data view, serialized IR, forged object or replacement Core/provider cannot restore a session.
binding.asset: The exact immutable input bytes and snapshot fix the asset and A/C/E binding. A handle does not acquire a new E or session field; the existing receiver binding and same snapshot enforce the applicable E correlation.
binding.epoch: Each Host incarnation has a fresh host_epoch. The trusted policy epoch is fixed for the session; epoch change, restart, revocation, disposal or expiry invalidates retained state. No persistence or cross-restart request deduplication is established.

admission_and_reuse.first_read: Use existing readNode with formal Read request admission and trusted control. Observe the actual snapshot through the original trusted Host provider and retain it only as pending until successful formal Read completion and actual delivery finish.
admission_and_reuse.subsequent_read: Use the existing public readBrowser(snapshot, candidate, control, originalHostProvider) path against the same real snapshot; preserve all formal Read admission, Host authorization, handle, disclosure, omission, mandatory-support, budget and diagnostic precedence rules.
admission_and_reuse.request_id_consumption: After formal Read admission, at the first eligible observation entering the trusted Host gate for the bound call, atomically reserve the validated request_id before continuing that gate. Binding, lifetime and capacity remain enforced; existing policy authorization and denial handling remain unchanged. Repeated observations within that call do not consume it again. Concurrent calls cannot reserve the same ID. An already reserved ID is not made reusable by denial or delivery failure. Requests rejected by formal Read before this observation preserve their earlier diagnostics and do not reserve an ID.
admission_and_reuse.duplicate: A duplicate validated request_id fails closed by throwing a fixed internal control failure through the existing Read pipeline, which maps it to READ_TRANSPORT_FAILURE (502/null body). It is not converted into an asset denial and must not spuriously latch asset denial. This adds no Read diagnostic.
admission_and_reuse.handle_reuse: A valid issued handle may be used again with a fresh admitted request_id under the same retained provider, binding, snapshot and current authorization. Handles are not single-use tokens. Only Read owns and checks the private issuance registry; Host must not substitute a parallel authority registry.
admission_and_reuse.denial: Keep the original provider and existing Read denial latch across calls. Retention cannot lift denial, broaden scope or bypass reauthorization.
admission_and_reuse.serialization: At most one snapshot and one in-flight read exist. Excess concurrency fails closed immediately without an unbounded queue, replacing the snapshot, or corrupting the active session. An unresolved noncooperative callback retains its in-flight charge; timeout cannot falsely free capacity for another operation.

delivery.commit: Node and Express commit an eligible result only after BOTH the real server response finish event and formal Read success for that same call. A generated body, successful write invocation, returned Response or client-side observation alone is insufficient.
delivery.failure: Close, error, abort, timeout, false delivery confirmation or failed formal Read cannot commit ready content or activate pending retention. Unconfirmed delivery terminates the enabled session. A bounded control result may be delivered without representing ready content. Already transmitted physical bytes cannot be recalled; failure is not proof of zero bytes sent.
delivery.proof_limit: Server finish proves completion at that server transport boundary; it is not remote receipt, remote acknowledgement or downstream consumption.
delivery.commit_recheck: Before and after trusted delivery, recheck that the instance remains open and its trusted binding, policy epoch and deadlines are valid. Only the original prepared Read result may proceed. Read alone registers handles after its successful delivery path; Host activates pending snapshot and bytes only after the formal call returns that successful ready result.

lifecycle.ttl: An absolute monotonic lifetime starts at first preparing after trusted context verification and bounded input capture. Reads and failures do not renew it. Provider context expires_at is no later than the earlier of the absolute session deadline and independent policy expiry; existing shorter handle/context validity remains enforced. Expiry or trusted clock rollback/invalidity closes the session.
lifecycle.terminal_cleanup: On expiry, bound-context revocation, policy epoch change, unconfirmed delivery, resource termination or disposal, invalidate eligibility first, then release available Host-owned input/snapshot references, queued work, timers and listeners. Keep unresolved in-flight work charged until settlement; release the original provider after its pending calls settle. Counters accurately distinguish released resources from unsettled external work. Closed is terminal and never returns to unbound.
lifecycle.external_callbacks: A noncooperative external callback cannot be forcibly freed. Cleanup guarantees removal of owned references and prevention of late commits, not forced garbage collection of independently retained external references.
transitions: disabled: retain existing stateless behavior; valid explicit configuration starts unbound.
unbound -> preparing: first trusted binding and bounded input capture set one absolute deadline and acquire the sole in-flight slot; formal readNode performs admission.
preparing -> delivering: formal Read projection and second Host check plus complete-envelope/resource budgeting prepare one intact result.
delivering -> active: actual server finish and successful formal Read return commit the pending real snapshot and original bytes.
active -> delivering -> active: same bytes, snapshot and original provider pass fresh formal readBrowser admission, Host checks and delivery; pending work never becomes visible early.
any enabled activity -> closed: expiry, trusted clock failure, bound revocation, epoch change, disposal, unconfirmed delivery or terminal resource failure; no automatic rebind or reopen.

limits.units: Bytes are octets. MiB is 1048576 bytes. All caps are hard per retained Host session unless explicitly scoped to a call; configurations may tighten but never raise the maxima.
limits.accounting: Check capacity before retention, reservation, issuance and delivery. The retained view charge is UTF-8 byte length of plain JSON serialization of the Core inspection data view; it is an accounting charge, not JCS, a semantic digest or precise heap usage. Handle accounting includes each retained issuance record and its bounded serialized charge. Complete final responses remain subject to formal Read byte budgeting. Bounds and safe integer validation precede allocations or timer scheduling.
limits.read_counting: Every read entry consumes the bounded attempt count, including rejects and timeouts, independently of the validated request-ID set. Failures never reset or renew the count.
limits.handle_accounting: Conservatively reserve count and UTF-8 serialized metadata charge for newly prepared handles before delivery, then commit the charge after formal successful delivery. Use pending/final result metadata for resource accounting only; do not copy, mutate, delete entries from or replace the Read-owned authority registry. Final provider disposal releases that registry as a whole after pending calls settle.
limits.outer_limits: Retained calls also preserve existing multipart 12 MiB, request JSON 64 KiB and Core input limits. Read final-envelope, HTTP-frame, retained accounting and total process memory are distinct limits; none proves the others.

acceptance_obligations: Independently exercise two successful real HTTP reads with a retained issued handle, fresh request IDs, same actual Core snapshot/provider, authorized scope and mandatory support.
Exercise duplicates, invalid and foreign binding, revocation, epoch change, stale or foreign handles, expiry, disposal, concurrent reads, capacity and every byte/count/time cap.
Exercise Node and Express finish plus formal success, close/error/abort/timeout and late callbacks; prove no premature or late ready-content commit and explicit Next retained rejection.
Recheck retained-session lifecycle/limits and wire/client surfaces under the new exact Core/IR/Read binding. Generator reproducibility does not discharge runtime or consumer obligations.

host_configuration.ownership: Only trusted embedding supplies configuration. Reject unknown fields and invalid values before starting retention. These are Host configuration descriptions, not additional Core/Read wire types or exports.

options_type.name: RetainedReadSessionOptions

required.verifyContext: (context: trusted current server context) => boolean | Promise<boolean>

options_type.validation: Identifier and UInt retain their existing public meanings. Positive UInt additionally excludes zero. maxHandleRecordBytes is the aggregate per-session record byte charge, not a per-record allowance. The effective maxReads also cannot exceed the existing Host lifetime read limit. Omitted optional values take the listed defaults; supplied values must not exceed the maxima.

host_configuration.policy: Retention configuration does not grant read permission. Missing or invalid observePolicy remains default deny. verifyContext must independently verify the fixed binding and authorization domain; matching configuration strings alone is insufficient.

host_surface.read: host.read(bytes, candidate, settings) keeps its signature. First call captures an independent bounded input copy. Later calls must byte-for-byte match the retained bytes without new Core admission or recomputation of A/C/E; a different input rejects and cannot replace the bound asset.
host_surface.dispose: host.dispose() and server.dispose() are idempotent terminal operations. They cannot reopen a session or retract physical bytes already sent.

retention_state.disclosure: Summary counters and state only; never snapshot, handles, binding keys, identities, input or payload. Counters confer no authority.

host_surface.express: The Express result remains callable middleware and forwards dispose() and retentionState(); these management methods do not create a network listener.
host_surface.stateless_helper: handleKDNARequest rejects enabled retention with Host-local HOST_RETAINED_INSTANCE_REQUIRED; a new instance per request cannot provide this profile.
host_surface.delivery_required: Direct Host/handle retained operation requires trusted settings.deliverResponse or the actual Express/Node finish boundary. Missing confirmation rejects with Host-local HOST_DELIVERY_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED.
host_surface.unsupported_next: Next rejects enabled retention with Host-local HOST_RETAINED_DELIVERY_UNSUPPORTED. The default-disabled path retains existing semantics.
host_surface.closed_instance: A closed retained instance rejects further calls with Host-local HOST_SESSION_CLOSED.
host_surface.error_namespace: These management/configuration failures stay Host-local. They are not ReadDiagnostic additions and cannot override an earlier formal Read error.

original_accepted_contract_baseline.surfaces: No new Core or Read primitive, export, diagnostic, schema field or wire tuple. No new HTTP route, session header, multipart field or Web Client API. Existing read/inspect transport and client exports remain unchanged.
non_claims: Remote identity or authorization derived from a client session_id
Global replay prevention or persistence across Host restarts
original_accepted_contract_baseline.client_lifecycle: Every client request uses a fresh caller-held association and the existing file/request transport. Client dispose/release/cancel is not remote revocation. The Host enforces its own expiry and trusted disposal. Existing credentials=omit is unchanged; no ambient credential or multi-tenant handshake is added.
original_accepted_contract_baseline.host_candidate_version: @aikdna/kdna-web-server@0.4.0-rc.host-session.1 is the implementation candidate coordinate. Its exact dependency graph must contain one Core 0.23.0 brand implementation and Read 0.2.0; version labels do not substitute for immutable package byte pins. This profile does not repack those upstream artifacts.

current_component_rebinding.scope: The retained-session lifecycle and limits remain unchanged. The historical Host artifact and its accepted exact graph are preserved at their original coordinates; they are not current evidence for component supply. Its actual successor must bind exactly one current Core/Read pair and independently preserve the complete method value, current Host gate, handles and full budgets. No new Host package or consumer acceptance is claimed here.

rules: Only actual WHATWG Response intrinsic state is inspected; response.url must exactly match caller endpoint_url and redirected/opaque/used bodies are rejected. Context is closed caller-held data, never a network identity or Host authority.

outbound_request_json is the exact JSON string caller sent as the HTTP request field. Its strict parsed candidate supplies request_id/mode/selection/handle/budget; context correlation must match. Invalid candidates can receive admission_rejection or header-only controls, never a ready envelope.

Association IDs are consumed once per process for their bounded lifetime across all endpoint/session claims. Expired contexts reject; capacity is bounded. A new association cannot establish network replay protection or remote identity. The association must remain unexpired through body consumption and final admission; reading is bounded by the smaller of max_read_ms and remaining association lifetime.

HTTP channels are read_envelope:200 ready/422 rejected; admission_rejection:422; no_body_control:413 no JSON/body; transport_failure:502 no JSON/body. Header-only controls preserve only observed headers, never synthesize remote correlation or delivery proof.

Body reads stop at both declared and actual byte bounds or timeout; UTF-8, duplicate keys, structural limits, exact JCS bytes and generated Schema are mandatory. Content encoding other than identity is unsupported. HTTP framing is checked only as exposed by native fetch, not as raw wire framing. WebKit-normalized Transfer-Encoding: Identity is accepted with bounded decoded bytes; Simultaneously visible Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding reject, including Identity.

Ready association verifies caller tuple/asset/A/C/E, optional expected snapshot, request/receipt and handle observable bindings, mode/selection and declared full-body counts. It does not recalculate Canonical IR or authorize the remote receipt or Host.

Every result has origin=remote, explicit proof scope/limits and literal false local capabilities. It never mints or reconstructs any local opaque brand. Unverifiable remote identity/signature/PKI/revocation/network replay/third-party Host/WKWebView remain NOT_PROVEN.

reference.relationship: Finite interpretation inherited; public carriers and declared Agent adoption mapping use this new public definition digest, never the reference digest as authority.

component.definition: Explicit adoption of KDNA public component semantics 1.0.0.

adoption.definition: Static component adoption record for KDNA public component semantics 1.0.0.

presence.definition: Authored method field presence for KDNA public component semantics 1.0.0.

rules: H(value) is SHA-256 of existing canonicalJson UTF-8 bytes, with sha256: prefix; object keys sort by UTF-16 code units, arrays preserve original order; finite strict Unicode JSON only. D_public=H(this entire definition record). It is distinct from the frozen reference D. No caller may replace profiles, grammar, rules or D_public.

Extension.value mechanically decodes SemanticValue to ordinary JSON; duplicate record field names reject. Exact named carrier schemas and exact id/location/critical/definition are mandatory. Registered ids at any wrong position or with false critical reject. Unregistered noncritical extensions remain opaque; unknown critical extensions block. Never recursively interpret arbitrary content field names as extension instructions.

Every component id remains a real unique protocol id, qualified by its owning judgment at creation. Item keys remain local keys, never converted to protocol ids or matched by title. Parent method is an actual non-null TermRef. Native known method requirements apply only without a TermRef extension: required component types and binding roles must be present. Unknown method terms are not inferred from components.

For each opt-in, judgment_ref names its actual owner; component_ref resolves uniquely among that judgment method components. Its native component.method.term equals the profile component type, and that component TermRef has no extension. Multiple same-type components, multiple distinct roles and legal unbound components are preserved.

All opt-in component bindings target_ref equal the owning judgment id and component_ref equal that component; exact duplicate binding records reject. H(bindings) sorts complete binding objects by role then target_ref using unsigned UTF-8 comparisons. bindings_digest covers all roles, including an explicitly empty list. Non-CS1 native binding targets keep existing semantics.

component_declaration_digest=H({component:the complete native MethodComponent,statement_origin}). Authored statement is preserved verbatim. For mechanical_content_representation only, statement equals canonicalJson(content) exactly; it is mechanically encoded content with original array order, not an additional authored assertion. Raw and repeated bytes count toward real container and Read budgets.

content_digest=H(content), preserving raw item/edge/contrast order. declaration_digest=H(the complete decoded component carrier). profile, type, D, content, native component/statement origin and all bindings must match before a supported interpretation is returned. adoption_proposal_digest is a static claim, not evidence that external adoption occurred.

All declared content objects are exact. Keys match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$. Title/meaning/prompt/criterion strings are nonempty, not all whitespace, have no leading/trailing whitespace, preserve exact Unicode and satisfy UTF-8 byte limits. Duplicate local keys reject; duplicate titles remain distinct. Item arrays declare sets, no order, preference, probability, chronology, causal sequence, exclusivity or exhaustiveness.

Taxonomy content is items plus broader edges. Each endpoint resolves locally; self edges, duplicate directed edges and directed cycles reject. Multiple parents are allowed. A path may contain at most64 directed edges (initial node depth0);65 edges reject. Reachability supplies declared inclusion meaning without inventing extra authored edges. Normalized body has kind taxonomy, items sorted by key and original broader edges sorted narrowerKey then broaderKey.

Candidate-set content is items. Explicit items=[] is a supported authored empty collection, not missing/unknown/deferred or a claim the real world has none. Normalized body has kind candidate-set and items sorted by key.

Discriminator content is candidateSetRef plus items. The ref names an actual same-judgment opt-in candidate-set component. Each item has key/title/prompt and at least2 distinct candidateKey/criterion contrasts resolving to that target. Omitted candidates are not excluded. Total contrasts count as relation edges. No candidate conditions are conjoined across candidates, evaluated or converted to outcomes. Normalized body includes kind discriminator-set, unchanged candidateSetRef, all target key/title pairs as sorted candidateIndex, sorted items and contrasts sorted by candidateKey.

At most256 native components in a Payload; at most128 items and1024 edges per component; canonical content <=65536 bytes each and all opt-in content <=196608 bytes. Existing parser/resource limits apply first. Limits reject without truncation or omission. Index all declarations and simple profiles before resolving discriminators; declaration input order cannot change resolution.

At most one presence carrier per judgment; actual parent method must exist, at least one field state must be undeclared, and its native corresponding array must be empty. Contradiction, redundant declared/declared, duplicate, wrong location/owner/state or noncritical carrier rejects. No presence carrier means native arrays are explicitly declared. Missing parent method remains absent. Presence-only without opt-in must not generate an empty adoption record.

Exactly one Payload component-adoption carrier exists iff at least one component opt-in exists. declaration_set_digest=H(all complete decoded component carrier values sorted by judgment_ref then component_ref in unsigned UTF-8 order). proposal_set_digest=H(sorted unique adoption_proposal_digest strings). D and contract identity must match; decision_digest is a claimed private decision digest and adoption_kind remains human_claim_unverified or delegated_agent_editorial. No static digest proves real identity, confirmation, permissions or strong Creation.

Formal creation retains two actual alternatives and real selected actor response, materials/interview/revision/final decision and complete candidate. A one-use host capability binds them before invoking Compiler. Versioned creation materialization kdna.studio-materialization/2 assigns judgment ids as judgment: plus lowercase full SHA-256 hex of canonicalJson([ruleId,"judgment",asset_id,judgmentLocalKey]); component ids as component: plus SHA-256 hex of canonicalJson([ruleId,"component",asset_id,judgmentLocalKey,componentLocalKey]), with ruleId kdna.studio-materialization/2 and existing canonicalJson UTF-8. Local keys match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$; duplicate local keys within their owner and any generated protocol-id collision reject without suffixing. Version is not an ID input but the complete candidate version remains bound by context. Core treats protocol ids as opaque and verifies actual ownership. The external expected materialization maps discriminator local references to those actual ids and includes original content/order/statement origin/all role targets/presence and every proposal/set/decision. After save, fresh public Core checks exact bytes against that external context. Re-signed compiler tampering and capability replay reject. Presence-only is compared even when expected component bindings are empty. An Agent editorial adoption is never relabeled human.

Core technical checks precede component interpretation. No opt-in gives undeclared with null body and no guessed semantics. Valid explicit empty content gives supported with empty arrays. Component interpretation failure yields Core valid and interpretation blocked, no snapshot/body disclosure and a named invalid component failure where applicable. Structural failure remains Core invalid; unknown critical meanings remain blocked without executing them.

The method IR value separates native declaration, declaration_presence and component_interpretations. All supported bodies, candidate indices, original content, statement provenance, roles and necessary source-use targets are mandatory for exact_selection. No deferred bodies in this version. Catalog and whole_asset keep current public mode meanings; whole_asset has asset declarations/catalog and no judgment closure. Unknown/denied/failed/not_in_mode are not empty collections.

Read uses the same Core projection and full final-envelope budget, real request/tuple/selection/snapshot binding, current Host scope/time/revocation and issued handles. No custom Reader interpreter, opaque fallback, partial criteria truncation or action permission. This public supply is not a claim to implement every private RS2 behavior.
